alan-sales: On the ACME hands-on right now. They triggered a sudden burst and we started getting 5xxs. They asked whether these errors mean their data was dropped — also asking about demo pricing if we give them reserved capacity for the week.
alan-sales: Can we triage quickly? Theyre still on the call.
tyler-support: Im looking at the interval 2026-03-21T09:40:00Z - 09:48:00Z. Spike from 300 rps -> ~1.8k rps. Errors started at ~09:41. Sample req id: req_b2c3d4e5.
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] autoscaler: scale-up requested at 2026-03-21T09:41:12Z, instance_provision_delay=22s, nodes_added=2 at 09:41:34Z.
maria-eng: Checking node logs for req_b2c3d4e5: one inference worker OOM'd while processing a 2.5k-token prompt; router queue hit 30/threshold 18 so router returned 503s after retry budget exhausted.
maria-eng: Snippet:
```
2026-03-21T09:41:11Z req_b2c3d4e5 INFO request.start tokens=2500 model=redwood-3b-ctx
2026-03-21T09:41:12Z worker-7 FATAL out-of-memory alloc_size=1.4GiB
2026-03-21T09:41:12Z router WARN queue_depth=30 > 18
```
josh-sre: Short fixes we can apply now: 1) soft concurrency cap for the demo (concurrency=80) 2) fallback to redwood-3b-compact which uses less memory 3) enable kv-cache prewarm for the session.
alan-sales: Customer wants two things: a) a short statement confirming no user content was retained in logs that would violate their privacy/security questionnaire, b) a cost estimate to keep a reserved node for the remainder of the POC week.
nina-security: For (a) we need to be careful. Logs contain request IDs and anonymized token counts. We do not store plaintext prompt content in long-term logs by default. If they want log bundles, we must scrub PII. Tyler, can you confirm what we captured in the expanded log bundle?
tyler-support: Confirmed: expanded logs include correlation ids, non-persistent request traces, and truncated prompt hashes. No full prompt text saved to persistent logging storage. For immediate customer reassurance I can provide a sanitized summary and an exported bundle with PII redaction.
alan-sales: Great. For (b) whatis the ballpark for a single N4 reserved instance for 5 days? I need a quote to give them.
maria-eng: For a short-term reserved demo node we can offer a "demo burst" pricing: flat fee $950/day for an N4 reserved node (including faster pre-pull and priority scheduling). This is below enterprise reserved pricing since it's temporary.
alan-sales: Noted. If they accept reserved node, will that prevent these 5xxs entirely for their workload?
maria-eng: It will greatly reduce the likelihood but not eliminate it. If their prompts stay large, a single node could still hit OOM if concurrency is high. Recommend combo: reserved node + concurrency cap + model-compact fallback.
josh-sre: Also suggest autoscaler tuning: reduce scale-up cool-down from 30s -> 10s for that pool, and enable image pre-pull; will open ENG-5501 to track.
tyler-support: Ill push the sanitized log bundle to the deal thread and flag nina-security for review.
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] routing-change: fallback model redwood-3b-compact applied to customer_acme_demo at 2026-03-21T09:43:15Z by maria-eng.
olivia-customer: Wesaw errors drop after the fallback, thanks. Still curious if you can guarantee data deletion from logs.
nina-security: We can provide a signed attestation: "no persistent storage of full prompt text without explicit export request." Also offer to perform a redaction run on the bundle before sharing.
alan-sales: Customer wants the attestation and a 3-line explainer for their security team. Tyler, can you draft now?
tyler-support: Drafting now: "Redwood Inference POC logs: request IDs, timestamps, and aggregate metrics captured. Full prompt text is not stored in persistent logs; exports require explicit action and will be redacted on request. Temporary debug captures for the incident were sanitized before sharing."
alan-sales: Perfect. Please upload that and the sanitized bundle. Also send the pricing note: demo-burst $950/day or can do a 5-day package at $4,000.
maria-eng: I created ENG-5501 (autoscale tuning), ENG-5502 (pre-pull job), and ENG-5503 (kv-cache warmup feature request) and linked them to the customer tag.
josh-sre: Postmortem summary I'll publish: root cause = rapid traffic ramp + large-context prompts -> worker OOMs -> router backlog -> 503s. Mitigation = concurrency cap + model fallback + reserved node option + autoscaler tuning. Follow-ups include alerting on router.queue_depth > 15 for >60s and adding a billing SKU for demo bursts.
alan-sales: Thanks all. Customer happy to accept fallback + sanitized attestation and wants the pricing options. Ill summarize and send an email.
olivia-customer: Thanks team 44d. We will review the attestation and confirm reserved node decision by EOD.
tyler-support: Uploading sanitized logs and attestation now to the deal thread.
maria-eng: Will monitor the pool for 24h and check ENG tickets tomorrow.
alan-sales: Closing loop here. If we see a repeat spike we'll consider the reserved node. Thanks everyone.
